votes.e: B/project/docs/metadata.md:37 "Metadata is resolved **once per published version**, on the server, and stored with that version. Requests never re-parse the HTML."; :92 "The wrapper renders the resolved title and icon in its server HTML (public and unlisted)"; :105 "The wrapper is server rendered for every visibility. Its `<head>` is built only from the stored metadata of the current published version"; :109-127 list the wrapper's <title>, icon, og:* and twitter:* tags. Sources are the saved HTML parsed statically (:44 "The `<title>` in the HTML, parsed statically without running any script"), not the person's script at request time or the inner document.

B/project/docs/metadata.md:26 "| Preview card | Full card: title, description, image | Full card: title, description, image | Generic Tessel card only |" and :27 "| `robots` | `index` | `noindex` | `noindex` |"; :31 "Unlisted pages get the full card because anyone holding the link can already open them, and preview fetchers ignore `noindex` anyway."

B/project/docs/metadata.md:132 "Private, and every response to someone who may not open the page (signed out, not a member, page removed, or no longer shared):" followed by :135-141 `<title>Tessel</title>` / og:title "Tessel" / og:image "{Tessel brand card}", and :144 "No description, no page title, no page icon, no page image." Side paths are covered too: :151 icon/card routes "Private, removed, or no longer shared: serve the generic Tessel image" and :160 the frame URL "Without a valid token the user-content origin returns the same content-free response".

The no-saves half is met (B/project/docs/metadata.md:84 "writes report success to the page but are never stored"; :166 "A page's writes are held until a person has interacted with the page frame"). The network/credential half is not. The only isolation rule for the headless render is :83 "no access to anything inside Tessel except the page's own user-content origin and the runtime". It says nothing about private or internal networks (RFC1918, cloud metadata endpoints) or about credentials, and it does not say whether the hostile page script may reach the open internet. The publish-time server fetch of author-chosen URLs has no restriction at all: :69 "External icons are fetched once by the server." and :74 "`og:image` or `twitter:image` declared in the HTML, copied into Tessel storage at publish time". The doc also never says where or how the generated 1200x630 card (:75) is rendered.

B/project/docs/metadata.md:74 "`og:image` or `twitter:image` declared in the HTML, copied into Tessel storage" ranks above :75 "A **generated card**: 1200×630, showing the Tessel mark, the word Tessel, and the resolved page title"; :77 "The generated card is the default. Nobody has to make an image".

blocking: [claude-fallback] SSRF at publish: B/project/docs/metadata.md:69 "External icons are fetched once by the server." and :74 copy author-declared `og:image`/`twitter:image` URLs into Tessel storage. There is no rule that blocks private, loopback, link-local, or metadata addresses, and no rule for redirects or DNS rebinding. A hostile author can point an icon at an internal endpoint. If the response passes the PNG/SVG/ICO/WebP check, Tessel stores it and serves it publicly from its own icon route.

[claude-fallback] The snapshot render has no network or credential isolation: B/project/docs/metadata.md:83 "runs a headless browser in an isolated job ... no access to anything inside Tessel except the page's own user-content origin and the runtime". Hostile author script runs on Tessel infrastructure with no stated block on internal or private networks beyond Tessel's own, and nothing says the job holds no credentials.

[claude-fallback] Edge caching contradicts revocation. B/project/docs/metadata.md:148 says "Each request checks the page's **current** visibility", but :150 makes those same routes "cacheable at the edge", and :29 lets the public/unlisted wrapper use a "Shared cache allowed, purged on republish or visibility change". Edge-cached hits never reach the origin's visibility check. Until the purge has propagated, a page just made private still serves its titled wrapper and card to preview fetchers, which brings back bug 233. :186 "They must return the generic card immediately" cannot hold under this caching.
